entire enable — Enable Entire in current repository
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

Existing git hooks are kept: each is moved to <hook>.pre-entire and runs after
Entire's hook.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Current repo: not auto-detectable here (no origin remote / detached HEAD); pass --repo explicitly.

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string        Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). In an existing repository it lists the configuration files to commit rather than committing them. Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

content.content:
entire repo mirror add — Mirror a repository onto one or more clusters
With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs. --cluster requires a <repo>.

With a <repo>, places it on every cluster named by --cluster — repeat the flag or comma-separate the hosts — in parallel, then waits for each to become usable. Pass --no-wait to return as soon as the placements are registered. Idempotent on (repo, cluster), so naming a cluster the repo is already on reports it rather than failing.

When --cluster is omitted, an interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a multi-select; non-interactive runs default to aws-us-east-2.entire.io.

With an /et/ ref, places replicas of an Entire-native repo and waits for each to be seeded. A native mirror goes in a region other than the repo's own, so only those clusters are offered and --cluster has no default there: non-interactive runs must name one.

Every cluster is attempted: one that fails does not stop the others, and the command exits non-zero naming the ones that did.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Examples:
entire repo mirror add
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /gh/octocat/hello-world --cluster aws-us-east-2.entire.io,aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
  entire repo mirror add /et/acme/web --cluster aws-eu-central-1.entire.io

Both done: the test repo has a real two-turn Mistral Vibe session, and Entire's service has indexed it. Codex's code review is still running.

## The real session
- **Repo:** private `alishakawaguchi/mistral-vibe-entire-demo`, cloned at `/Users/alisha/Projects/test-repos/mistral-vibe-entire-demo`.
- **Web:** it should be at https://entire.io/gh/alishakawaguchi/mistral-vibe-entire-demo. I built that URL from the frontend's route layout and have not opened it in a browser.
- **Session:** `83805477-9abc-0f1f-31f3-3725a8d1a27a`, checkpoint `9344a0977bf0`, on commit `0a38668`. Vibe wrote a FizzBuzz script, ran it, then added a docstring and README usage in a second turn.
- **Recorded:** both prompts, the file-write and shell tool calls, the replies, 76k tokens, and the two touched files. `entire search "FizzBuzz"` returns the session from the server.

To get it onto entire.io I ran three things beyond creating the repo:
- installed the agent binary to `~/go/bin`;
- ran `entire enable --agent mistral-vibe` in the new repo;
- onboarded the repo with `entire repo mirror add` on `aws-us-east-2`, the cluster your other test repos use. This is reversible with `entire repo mirror remove`.

## Changes needed in entire.io
None are required. An unknown external agent is shown under its own name, "Mistral Vibe", with the default colour and no logo, and the per-agent transcript parsers were removed in August, so nothing is needed to render the transcript.

To give it a logo and colour like Goose or Kiro, four places change:
- `frontend/src/lib/agents.ts`: add an agent id and config, plus an alias so the name "Mistral Vibe" resolves to it.
- `frontend/public/images/logos/agents/`: add the SVG.
- `frontend/src/index.css`: add the `agent-…` colour class in the two places the others are defined.
- `api/src/routes/me.ts`: add the id to the agent enum and the per-agent counts, then regenerate the OpenAPI mocks.

The repo settings page's agent-configuration list only covers built-in agents (no Kiro, Amp or Goose), so it needs nothing.

## Seen in the real run
- **Stale Vibe setting:** Vibe prints "`hooks` is not a Vibe setting" on every run. That is the leftover `[hooks]` table from the old fork in your `~/.vibe/config.toml`; removing it stops the warning.
- **Resume ordering:** on `vibe -c`, the turn-start hook reached Entire one second before session-start. The checkpoint was still recorded correctly.

Want me to make the entire.io logo change? I'd need an SVG of the Mistral Vibe mark, or your go-ahead to source the official one.

Yes, that page is what the adapter is expected to produce. I checked each figure against the stored checkpoint:

| On the page | Stored | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Grey "Mistral Vibe" badge, no logo | agent `Mistral Vibe` | expected until the entire.io logo change is made |
| `mistral-medium-3.5` | same | correct |
| 3 tool calls, then 4 | write + 2 shell runs; 2 reads + 2 writes | correct |
| 1 checkpoint | two turns condensed into one commit | correct |
| 2 file changes, +19 | `README.md`, `fizzbuzz.py` | correct |
| 14.9K tokens | 13,828 input + 1,086 output | correct |
| Both prompts and both replies | present | correct |

Two things that might look off but are consistent:

- **14.9K vs the 76k I quoted earlier:** the CLI figure includes 61,056 cached input tokens; the web figure leaves them out. Both come from the same stored numbers.
- **No reasoning shown:** the adapter drops Vibe's reasoning entries from the compact transcript by design.

One thing I can't vouch for: the commit row shows the `Entire-Checkpoint: 9344a0977bf0` trailer inline after the commit subject. That comes from the web's commit rendering, not the agent, and I haven't checked whether other agents' sessions look the same.

One small inaccuracy that isn't visible on this page: the stored API call count is 9, because the adapter counts each tool call and each reply. Vibe ran two pairs of tool calls in parallel, so the real number of model calls is lower.

Codex's review is done, and its verdict is **not ready to push**: three blocking defects. I checked the first two against Vibe's source and both are real.

**Blocking**
1. **Long sessions lose history.** With no cursor, Vibe returns the newest 500 history entries and no next page, so anything older is silently dropped and stored line offsets shift. The unit test's fake server encoded my wrong assumption. Confirmed.
2. **Forked and rewound sessions are ignored.** I filter out every payload with a parent session id as a subagent, but Vibe sets a fork's parent to its source session, so every hook for it is dropped. Confirmed.
3. **A symlinked `.vibe` directory redirects hook edits outside the repo.** I only check the final `hooks.toml` for symlinks, not its parent directory, so install and uninstall could write to or delete a file elsewhere. I have not checked this one against the code yet.

**Should fix**
4. **Turn-end / session-end ordering is not guaranteed.** If the turn-end hook is slow to write its marker, session-end still goes first. The 30s wait and 20s fetch timeout also exceed Vibe's 5s quit budget.
5. **TOML block editing has holes.** A quoted `"hooks" = []` slips past the inline-array check, and marker text inside a user's string is treated as the managed block.
6. **Hooks fail under PowerShell.** The generated command is POSIX shell; Vibe on native Windows can run hooks through PowerShell.
7. **File permissions widen.** Install and uninstall rewrite an existing `hooks.toml` as 0644, even if it was 0600.
8. **API call count is inflated**, as noted on the web page check.
9. **The e2e adapter never cleans up its private Vibe home.**

**Unverified concerns** it raised: concurrent refreshes overwriting each other, and the 3-second freshness shortcut reusing a stale transcript on a fast next turn.

It confirmed that line-based offsets match what the CLI passes, that the parent-PID assumption holds, and that compaction handles sliced files correctly. It could not run the vet, compliance or live tests in its sandbox.

I'm starting on the fixes now, test-first, beginning with the three blockers.

fix(mistral-vibe): address review findings

Blocking:
- History paging dropped everything before the newest 500 entries. With
  no cursor Vibe returns the newest page whatever direction is asked
  for; page backward from it and reassemble oldest first.
- Forked and rewound sessions were ignored. Their parent_session_id is
  the source session, so that field alone does not mean "subagent".
  session_start and pre_agent (match = "main") are always tracked; a
  turn end or session end for an unknown child session is a subagent's.
- A symlinked .vibe directory was followed, so install and uninstall
  could write or delete a hooks file outside the repository. Refuse it.

Also:
- Turn-end/session-end ordering: turn start now marks the turn open, so
  session end waits for a turn-end hook that has not started yet.
  Waits and the session-end fetch are bounded to fit Vibe's 5s
  shutdown limit.
- hooks.toml: markers only count as whole lines, a quoted inline
  "hooks" key is refused, and an existing file keeps its permissions.
- API call count is per model response, not per tool call.
- VIBE_APP_SERVER_BIN must be absolute; bound the wait for the app
  server's pipes.
- e2e: reuse one private Vibe home instead of leaving one per run.
- Document that Windows needs Git Bash and that the ordering race is
  narrowed, not closed.

Each defect was reproduced with a failing test first. Unit tests, the
46 compliance tests and the 6 passing live lifecycle tests still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED

fix(mistral-vibe): address review findings

Blocking:
- History paging dropped everything before the newest 500 entries. With
  no cursor Vibe returns the newest page whatever direction is asked
  for; page backward from it and reassemble oldest first.
- Forked and rewound sessions were ignored. Their parent_session_id is
  the source session, so that field alone does not mean "subagent".
  session_start and pre_agent (match = "main") are always tracked; a
  turn end or session end for an unknown child session is a subagent's.
- A symlinked .vibe directory was followed, so install and uninstall
  could write or delete a hooks file outside the repository. Refuse it.

Also:
- Turn-end/session-end ordering: turn start now marks the turn open, so
  session end waits for a turn-end hook that has not started yet.
  Waits and the session-end fetch are bounded to fit Vibe's 5s
  shutdown limit.
- hooks.toml: markers only count as whole lines, a quoted inline
  "hooks" key is refused, and an existing file keeps its permissions.
- API call count is per model response, not per tool call.
- VIBE_APP_SERVER_BIN must be absolute; bound the wait for the app
  server's pipes.
- e2e: reuse one private Vibe home instead of leaving one per run.
- Document that Windows needs Git Bash and that the ordering race is
  narrowed, not closed.

Each defect was reproduced with a failing test first. Unit tests, the
46 compliance tests and the 6 passing live lifecycle tests still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
